title: Annotatio VI §.V (1): spiritual food nourishes faith — only self-proving believers, not Impious
pass_a_gloss: Nay, it is spiritual food only Nutritive, Augmentative, Corroborative, feeding and increasing faith, not conferring and imparting faith’s beginning: Hence it is enjoined to be received by those alone who can prove themselves, whether they are in faith — and after instituted examination find themselves to be in faith, though weak — not by others who either cannot prove themselves (as Infants) or examining themselves are convinced by conscience of their Impiety and impenitence (as the impious).
pass_b_english: Spiritual food only nourishes, augments, and corroborates faith — it does not plant faith’s start.

So it is commanded only for those who can prove they are in faith (even weak faith after self-examination) — not infants who cannot prove themselves, nor the Impious whose conscience convicts them of impenitence.
source_text: Quin, est spiritualis cibus, tantum Nutritivus, Augmentativus, Corroborativus, fidem alens & augens, non initium fidei conferens & impertiens: Hinc illis solis injunctus accipi, qui se ipsos probare possunt, num in fide sint? & post explorationem institutam, se in fide, imbecili licèt, deprehendunt esse, non aliis, qui vel se probare nequeunt ipsos, quales sunt Infantes, vel explorantes se, de Impietate ac impœnitentia sua per conscientiam convincuntur, quales sunt impii.
